Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border digital payment functionality is present but not fully on the instant payment rail: Orange Money Morocco indicates ability to “Receive money from abroad” in its app listing, and also allows transfers to/from a bank account. ([Google Play – Orange Money Maroc](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.orange.orangemoney&hl=en_US)) This supports partial cross‑border capability via specific providers rather than fully integrated national IPS cross‑border.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original single source (Orange Money app listing) describes a private mobile-money operator's international remittance receipt feature, not the national instant payment system, and does not support a score of 4. Authoritative sources (PAPSS/Afreximbank, 7 July 2025) confirm Bank Al-Maghrib only just signed the PAPSS membership agreement, becoming its 17th member country, with no evidence yet of live cross-border instant transactions. Downgraded to 3 (Under development) to reflect a newly-signed connection rather than functioning cross-border capability.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Evidence of active G2P digitization via programs exists, but this run did not collect a primary official Moroccan government document confirming electronic G2P disbursement at scale. A World Bank press release states implementation of digital management and payments for Morocco’s largest cash transfer program, Tayssir, providing subsidies to 3 million school children, helping lay foundation for social protection reform. ([World Bank press release](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/04/03/world-bank-continues-to-support-morocco-s-financial-and-digital-inclusion-reforms))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. A December 2024 World Bank press release confirms Morocco's Direct Social Benefit programme (launched December 2023) digitally disburses cash transfers to over half the population via the National Population/Social Registry, and Bank Al-Maghrib's National Financial Inclusion Strategy reports (2021-22) document ongoing digitisation of the Tayssir cash-transfer programme since 2020. Value 3 (Yes - Active Use) confirmed with stronger, more current sourcing than the single 2023 press release originally cited.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Morocco has a general consumer protection law (Law No. 31‑08) providing consumer rights and remedies, including for services. (Evidence from general sources was not collected to an official Moroccan legal text in this run.) For payments specifically, Bank Al‑Maghrib states it defines minimum safety requirements and fights fraud for cashless payment instruments, aiming to provide users with reliable and secure payment instruments. ([Bank Al‑Maghrib supervision of cashless payment instruments](https://www.bkam.ma/en/Systems-and-means-of-payment/Cashless-payment-instruments-and-their-monitoring/Monitoring-payment-instruments/Supervision-of-cashless-payment-instruments)) Given the lack of an official, specific payments consumer protection regulation text found during this run, score is set to partial.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial. Law No. 31-08 (2011, verified via WIPO Lex) is a general consumer protection law that extends to distance-payment contracts, and Bank Al-Maghrib Circular 7/W/16 (2016, amended 2022) regulates payment-service-provider conduct (KYC, account ceilings), but neither constitutes a dedicated payment-specific consumer-protection regime covering liability allocation and dispute resolution for unauthorised transactions. Year updated to reflect Law 31-08 (2011) rather than 2004.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Morocco has general data protection legislation: Law No. 09‑08 (18 Feb 2009) on protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data, implemented by Decree No. 2‑09‑165 (21 May 2009), enforced by the CNDP; it applies broadly to personal data processed by organizations including financial/payment providers. ([DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World – Morocco](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=MA))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via re-fetch of DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World: Law No. 09-08 (2009) and Decree 2-09-165 provide general, sector-neutral data protection; no specific payment-data provisions identified. Value 2 (General Data Protection Legislation) confirmed. Could not find an independent second source in this run to fully corroborate — flagged for human review to add a citation from the CNDP (Morocco's DPA) or UNCTAD's Cyberlaw Tracker.

Comments: Public performance reporting exists at least annually: Morocco’s central bank publishes annual reports including statistics and trends for payment instruments and systems (e.g., Bank Al‑Maghrib annual report PDFs include statistical appendices and chapters on payment modernization). ([Bank Al‑Maghrib Annual Report 2019 (PDF)](https://www.bkam.ma/en/content/download/711070/8207238/BAM-RA19-ENG.pdf))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and refreshed. Bank Al-Maghrib continues to publish its 'Rapport annuel sur les infrastructures des marchés financiers et les moyens de paiement et leur surveillance' annually, with editions through 2024 (published November 2025) and a detailed 2023 edition containing transaction volume/value statistics for interbank transfers, cheques, cards and the new instant-transfer platform (PCVI, launched June 2023). Value 3 (Annual) confirmed with a far fresher source than the 2019 report originally cited.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Morocco’s National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) is a government/central bank program (launched by Bank Al‑Maghrib and Ministry of Economy & Finance) aimed at expanding inclusion and uses digital payments as an entry point; it explicitly targets underserved groups (women, rural, unbanked) and discusses digitizing G2P/P2G flows as next steps. ([UNSGSA country visit write‑up](https://www.unsgsa.org/country-visits/morocco-has-opportunity-harness-digital-payments-fintech-and-green-finance-expand-financial-inclusion)) This establishes a formal inclusion governance mechanism tied to payments.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with stronger primary sourcing. Official National Financial Inclusion Strategy (SNIF) governance reports (Bank Al-Maghrib/ACAPS, 2021 and 2022 editions) document a National Financial Inclusion Council (CNIF), a Strategic Committee chaired by the BAM Governor, and a Steering/Coordination Committee with working groups, explicitly covering rural populations, women and digitisation of G2P payments (e.g. Tayssir). Value 3 (Yes) confirmed.
